gap: No result ChatGPT got (among the pages that opened) states that a 16-inch 2560x1600 panel has no clean macOS mode matching the MacBook Pro 16's interface size: 2x gives 'looks like 1280x800' with everything about 35% larger, native 2560x1600 is about 33% smaller and not Retina, and the in-between sharp mode needs the BetterDisplay app, per Parkablogs' Teoh Yi Chie.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's Mac roundup (cited) and PCWorld's roundup (cited), both opened 2026-11-26. Macworld gives no ppi, no macOS scaling or 'looks like' figure and no wattage; it lists the Duex Float 2 Pro only as 2560x1600 at 120 Hz, up to 350 nits, 2.9 lb. PCWorld says only that small size raises pixel density, with no ppi values and nothing on macOS. ChatGPT's own answer has part of it (2.5K 'a good compromise', 4K at 2x 'looks like 1920x1200') but not the 2.5K-side numbers, the app dependency or a measured-versus-claimed brightness figure. Not compared: RTINGS (page body is script-rendered, only navigation came back), TechRadar (cut off after the first pick) and seattlepi (fetch blocked), so one of those could hold part of this.
decides: It qualifies the 2560x1600 / 120 Hz line and leaves its order alone. Every 16-inch 2.5K row shares the same 188.68 ppi, so the footnote applies equally to the UPERFECT, SOTSU and Duex Float 2 Pro rows and does not reorder them; the page should say what the buyer gets on stock macOS (bigger-and-sharp or smaller-and-soft) and that MacBook-size sharp text needs BetterDisplay Pro at $21.99, or a 4K panel that drops the 120 Hz match. Separately, the one named-reviewer measurement on this UPERFECT 16-inch 120 Hz line came in at 238 nits against the maker's 400 cd/m2 (59.5%), so brightness must not rank the rows on listing claims alone, and the 120 Hz UPERFECT should carry the measured figure, not 350 or 400. The store pages could not be re-read today, so the desk's pick (GR16EQ) is neither confirmed nor changed by me.

findings.label: MacBook Pro 16 built-in display, the reference for the match
findings.value: 16.2 in, 3456 x 2234 at 254 ppi, ProMotion up to 120 Hz
findings.note: Apple's figures. At 2x Retina that is 1728 x 1117 points at 127 points per inch (3456/2, 2234/2, 254/2: my arithmetic).

findings.label: MacBook Pro 16 battery and charger
findings.value: 99.6 Wh battery (sold as 100 Wh), 140 W USB-C adapter in the box
findings.note: Apple's footnote gives 99.6 Wh. A 65 W pass-through port (Macworld's figure for the Duex Float 2 Pro) is 46% of the 140 W adapter (65/140).

findings.label: 16-inch 2560x1600 panel normalised to the MacBook's interface size
findings.value: 188.68 ppi, 74% of the MacBook's 254 ppi. At 2x: looks like 1280 x 800, 94.3 points/in, interface about 35% larger than the MacBook's and 53% of its workspace. At 1x: looks like 2560 x 1600, 188.7 points/in, interface about 33% smaller, one pixel per point (not Retina). Matching 127 points/in needs about 1723 x 1077 points, a 1.49x non-integer scale.
findings.note: Arithmetic on Apple's 254 ppi: sqrt(2560^2+1600^2)=3018.87 px / 16.0 in = 188.68 ppi; 127/94.34=1.346; 127/188.68=0.673; (1280x800)/(1728x1117)=0.53; panel is 13.57 x 8.48 in, x127 = 1723 x 1077. Applies to every 16.0-inch 2560x1600 row (UPERFECT GR16EQ and GR16DQ, SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16, Duex Float 2 Pro, Fold 16 QHD) if the diagonal is exactly 16.0 in.

findings.label: 4K-class panels on the same scale, for contrast
findings.value: 16-inch 3840 x 2400: 283.0 ppi, at 2x looks like 1920 x 1200 at 141.5 points/in, interface about 10% smaller than the MacBook's. 15.6-inch 3840 x 2160: 282.4 ppi, at 2x looks like 1920 x 1080 at 141.2 points/in.
findings.note: Arithmetic: 4528.3 px / 16 = 283.0; 4405.8 px / 15.6 = 282.4; 127/141.5 = 0.90. These panels (SOTSU Elite 16, espresso Pro 15, ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED) are 60 Hz per ChatGPT's answer and the desk notes, so they sit outside the 120 Hz line; their own spec pages were not opened.

findings.label: Sharp macOS scaling: stock or app
findings.value: Needs the BetterDisplay app: 'MacOS users will need an app called BetterDisplay for proper (sharp) UI scaling because MacOS does not work well with QHD & QHD+ resolution on a 16-inch display'
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Named reviewer's judgement on a 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz unit supplied by UPERFECT. The statement is about the resolution and size, so it carries to the other 16-inch 2.5K rows. The quote is joined from two excerpts the fetch returned; check the wording against the page before printing it.

findings.label: Cost of the app that adds the in-between sharp mode
findings.value: BetterDisplay Pro $21.99 one-time (perpetual licence), 14-day free trial; flexible HiDPI scaling is a Pro feature
findings.note: Developer's own page. It confirms the feature and price; it does not itself state the macOS limitation.

findings.label: Brightness, maker's claim against a named reviewer's measurement
findings.value: 400 cd/m2 claimed in the spec list; 238 nits measured maximum (59.5% of the claim)
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: 238/400 = 0.595. Parkablogs does not name the measuring tool or setting; it says an LG Gram Style 2023 powered the screen to 100% brightness over one USB-C cable. This is a 2023 unit sold as UPlays C2. I link it to today's GR16DQ only because its 0.72 kg and 12 W match the desk notes for that store page, which I could not re-read today; treat the model match as a lead.

findings.label: Weight, rated power and pass-through
findings.value: Net weight 0.72 kg (1.59 lb); rated power 12 W; pass-through charging 'less than 10W'
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: The 0.72 kg and 12 W are from the spec list on the review page; the text says 'the display weighs 720g' and mentions a folio case without saying whether it is included. 12 W is a rated figure, not a measurement: against the MacBook's 99.6 Wh it is 12% of the battery per hour for the screen alone (12/99.6). The pass-through is too small to charge a 16-inch MacBook Pro.

findings.label: Specs as Macworld lists them
findings.value: 16 in, 2560 x 1600 at 120 Hz, up to 350 nits, 2.9 lb (1.3 kg), 65 W pass-through
findings.note: Macworld's spec list. It does not say whether the 2.9 lb includes the stand, and 'up to 350 nits' is the maker's figure, not a measurement. Same 188.68 ppi and the same scaling footnote as the other 2.5K rows.

findings.label: How a rival states weight with and without the stand
findings.value: Plugable 15.6-inch: 1.85 lb (840 g) with cover/stand, 1.35 lb (615 g) without, a 0.5 lb (225 g) gap
findings.note: The only weight in the opened rival pages given both ways. It shows the size of the gap to expect when one maker quotes the panel alone and another the panel with its stand; a 1080p 60 Hz screen, outside this page's line.
